qt: to the Commission Asger Christensen (Renew) Subject:

Does the Commission take the view that, where a project or activity falls within the scope of Article 4(7) of the Water Framework Directive, for example as a ‘sustainable human development activity’, the Member State is required to assess whether the exemption applies, and to state why it does or does not apply?

Does the Commission take the view that the EU’s objectives as regards strategic autonomy, security of supply, food security, reducing dependence on third countries and maintaining and developing sustainable production capacity in the Union may, following a specific assessment, be regarded as considerations that fulfil the conditions for overriding public interest or sustainable development under Article 4(7) of the WFD?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.11.2026) Before authorising a project that may affect a water body, the Member State must assess whether the project complies with the requirements of Article 4 of the Water Framework Directive (WFD)1. As clarified by the Court of Justice of the EU2, a project must in principle be refused if it may cause a deterioration in the status of a surface water body or jeopardise the achievement of good water status. This requires a preliminary assessment of the project’s potential impacts on water. Article 4(7) of the WFD provides for a derogation from the obligation under Article 4(1) of the WFD under strict conditions. Where a new project is expected to deteriorate the status of a water body or prevent the achievement of the Directive’s environmental objectives for that water body, the Member State must establish on a case-by-case basis, whether all the conditions for applying Article 4(7) are fulfilled, before the project can be authorised, in particular whether the benefits to the environment and to society of achieving the objectives set out in paragraph 1 are outweighed by the benefits of the new modifications or alterations to human health, to the maintenance of human safety or to sustainable development. Where this derogation is used, the reasons for authorising the project must be set out in the relevant River Basin Management Plan. The justification should be sufficiently detailed and should explain, in particular, the measures taken to mitigate the project's adverse effects and to achieve the best possible status of the water body.
1 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a framework for Community
action in the field of water policy, OJ L OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, pp. 1–73. 2 C-461/13, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62013CJ0461.
